summary: A cardholder with no previous balance makes a single purchase during the billing cycle, stays within the credit limit, receives a statement, and pays the full statement balance before the due date. The scenario exercises the on-time full-payment path, showing that the minimum payment obligation is satisfied, the purchase grace period is preserved, and no late or over-limit fee is triggered.
assumptions: The account begins the cycle with no previous balance, so the purchase qualifies for the contract's grace-period condition on new purchases.
The cardholder makes only one domestic purchase in this cycle and no cash advances, balance transfers, returned payments, or international transactions occur.
The issuer sends the statement on the statement closing date shown below, and the stated due date is 25 days later, satisfying the contract's minimum grace-period timing for purchases.
A payment equal to the full new balance is received and credited on the same day it is made because it is submitted through a standard approved payment method on a business day.

To satisfy the modeled credit-limit obligation in this archetype, the purchase event is explicitly bound to clause-4-credit-limit and is assumed to represent card use that remains within the disclosed credit limit.
No fees are assessed in this cycle because the balance never exceeds the credit limit on the statement date and payment is made on or before the due date.
